ceiling_directive: Prove that every all-branches failure yields, on the same input COPAG and target, a represented residual-forest family passing the denominator-lock rank test, and integrate that construction into the advertised output-sensitive certificate algorithm.
improvement_directive: Complete the graph-to-lock implication: starting from an arbitrary all-branches-fail role graph, construct a represented one- or two-mechanism rational tangent with E_T q = 0 and b_T q != 0, then prove the claimed O(3^n poly(n) + L_Gamma) synthesis bound.
critique: The advertised denominator-locked completeness and formula-or-checkable-failure procedure are not proved: AllFail is explicitly given no nonidentification implication, and the graph-to-lock step remains open. The affine compiler only converts a supplied represented family, legal trace, forest pair, and successful rank condition into a certificate; it does not show that any of these inputs exist after Branch-sCIDP fails. The selection-equalizer lift and connected binary example establish exact locked witnesses on specially constructed graphs, not certificates for arbitrary failing input COPAGs or the fixed target under analysis. Branch-sCIDP itself contributes sound exhaustive search and cache accounting on top of published soundness, so the delivered package is a useful but narrow companion result rather than a new identification theorem. The framing is substantially faithful, but the proposed PAGId formula-or-checkable-failure consumer remains unsupported, limiting both significance and reproducible practical value. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
